meta.title: Li & Lumb (1987) homogeneous slope, rᵤ = 0.2
meta.notes: 10 m high 1:1 slope (Li & Lumb's illustrative example, Fig. 5) with the means of their random variables: c′ = 18 kPa, tan φ′ = tan 30°, γ = 18 kN/m³, rᵤ = 0.2; critical-circle search. The ground 5 m below and beyond the toe and 5 m behind the crest is a program manual's model; the critical circle passes through the toe.

source.reference: Li, K.S. & Lumb, P. (1987). Probabilistic design of slopes. Can. Geotech. J. 24(4), 520–535; Hassan, A.M. & Wolff, T.F. (1999). J. Geotech. Geoenviron. Eng. 125(4), 301–308.
source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V101 (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: Li & Lumb (1987), p. 9 and Fig. 5: the slope (10 m, 1:1) and the moments c′ 18 kPa (COV 20 %), γ 18 kN/m³ (5 %), t = tan φ′ = tan 30° (10 %), rᵤ 0.2 (10 %), with ũᵢΔxᵢ = rᵤ·Aᵢγ̄ᵢ (eq. 29), cSlope's rᵤ. They print no factor of safety; their βHL = 2.50 (Hasofer–Lind, with spatial averaging).

Hassan & Wolff (1999), Table 7 and Fig. 13: on the critical deterministic surface A, FS 1.334 and lognormal β 2.336; surfaces B–E 1.190 … 1.360 are the critical surfaces found with one parameter at a time set one standard deviation off its mean. They do not name the method for this example (their other examples use Bishop and Spencer); both program manuals run it with Bishop. cSlope: Spencer 1.332, M-P (half-sine) 1.330.

cSlope's critical circle (4.063, 19.410, R 14.441) runs from the toe to the crest 2.8 m behind its edge, as Hassan & Wolff's Fig. 13 draws surface A. Commercial program A (verification problem 36) and commercial program B (§2.23) are compared on their own searched surfaces.
cSlope fija options.tolerance = 0.001 (tolerancia del solver) en sus checks; no se importa: ogs usa analysis.tolerance = 1e-05.
